newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks off on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks off on profit taking.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks fell on profit taking Tuesday, as the market tracked a retreat in bonds after two sessions of big gains.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 17.02 points at 5,716.82 following Monday's jump of 74 points and Friday's rise of 53 points.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances 11-9 on moderate volume of 222 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index was off 1.67 to 1,147.04. The American Stock Exchange index was up 2.07 to 564.03.
"It's very basically profit-taking. The market got too far ahead of itself yesterday," said Kenneth Ducey, director of trading at Bankers Trust's BT Brokerage.
In the bond market, the 30-year Treasury bond lost 19/32 of a point, and its yield, which moves in the opposite direction to its price, rose to 7.12 percent from Monday's close of 7.07 percent.

"We have a good framework now," said Joseph Battipaglia, chief investment officer at Gruntal & Co. "There's great comfort among investors that buying on a dip is still the right strategy and the economy is still on track, he said.

"Money is still pouring into funds, providing fuel for the fire. Plus, we've had interesting merger proposals which generate interest. It's a matter of consolidation more than anything else," Battipaglia said.
He believes that blue-chips will lead the market with small stocks trailing.

"The second and tertiary stocks, which were out front for the beginning of the year, went into a terrible slide. The IPO market has been slow to come back," Battipaglia said. "You need to have the drivers of earnings and revenue growth. (The smaller caps) will be tracking the market, but not as high."

Among individual stocks, ITT Corp. was under siege, dropping 7-7/8 to 48-1/8 after it warned that its third quarter results will fall below expectations on weak casino revenue, particularly at its Las Vegas operations.
The Big Three automakers fell after Ford Motor Co. disclosed that its financial performance in Brazil in the second half of the year would be "substantially worse" than the first half.

Ford was down 1 to 30-1/4 in heavy trading. General Motors Corp., which also has substantial Brazilian operations, fell 7/8 to 47-3/8. Chrysler Corp., which recently announced a $315 million plan for its first Brazilian assembly plant, dropped 3/4 to 28.
